fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential banking regulation and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF and cross-border transaction surveillance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a freely floating and fully convertible currency with no general exchange-control restrictions on current-account payments, capital-account transfers, profit repatriation, dividend distributions, or capital liquidation. Non-resident dividend and interest remittances are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25%), with applicable treaty relief (e.g., Canada-United States, Canada-China, Canada-Hong Kong, Canada-India treaties). In Quebec, corporations must satisfy the solvency test under the Quebec Business Corporations Act before declaring dividends. No government approval is required for routine cross-border capital flows; the Investment Canada Act applies only to acquisitions of control of Canadian businesses, not to operating capital injections or treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio. Canadian exporters may retain export receipts in foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts. For income tax purposes, eligible corporations may elect a functional currency under section 261 of the Income Tax Act, but this does not impose any FX surrender or central-bank conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Foreign fintech entities and electronic money institutions are not authorized to carry on deposit-taking business under the Bank Act. They may only operate in Canada as registered payment service providers or through partnership with a Schedule I Canadian bank, subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act registration and safeguarding obligations. For immigration-visa advisory operations involving client funds, escrowed program fees, and government application pass-throughs, the use of an offshore EMI as the primary treasury rail creates material legal, AML, licensing, and reputational risk. The recommended structure is a regulated Canadian bank account with an EMI used only for FX benchmarking or non-client ancillary disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Neither federal law nor Quebec law mandates physical board-director appearance as a statutory condition. FINTRAC requires regulated financial entities to apply risk-based client identification. Remote account opening is feasible using corporate registry excerpts, notarized resolutions, digital identity verification, and video interviews. In practice, Schedule I banks often require at least one Canadian-resident director or authorized signatory to attend an in-branch verification for non-resident-owned corporations. For Quebec-registered entities, the Registraire des entreprises profile can be used as the primary identity document. A physical Quebec office presence materially de-risks onboarding and allows branch interview accommodation when requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident foreign-controlled corporation with opaque beneficial ownership or nominees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Federal/Quebec incorporation certificates; Registraire des entreprises certificate; current register of directors and shareholders; FINTRAC beneficial-ownership declaration; notarized corporate resolutions; sworn source-of-wealth letters; passports of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; independent legal opinion confirming control structure and absence of nominees; preceding 90-day bank statements of principal shareholders

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large upfront global-immigration or study-abroad commissions, third-party payments from relatives, or payments representing government visa/application fees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client service agreements; published fee schedule; itemized invoices; proof of status as a licensed immigration consultant or lawyer under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) regime; escrow/trust accounting ledger; client source-of-funds documentation; evidence that government fees are pass-through and never commingled with operating revenue; explanation of refund policies

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed persons (PEPs), sanctioned territories, or crypto-linked sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file; PEP and sanctions screening results for each client; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; evidence of independent verification of client identity; legal opinion on sanctions compatibility; FINTRAC large transaction reporting records; internal decision memorandum approving or rejecting the relationship with stated rationale

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions should be routed using SWIFT MT103 or the ISO 20022 pacs.008 equivalent to the Canadian bank account with the beneficiary legal name, bank BIC, account number, and remittance information clearly stating 'Equity Injection / Share Subscription / Ref: [corporate resolution date and number]'. No exchange-control permit is required; however, Canadian banking institutions are obligated to report electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. The foreign investor should provide the share subscription agreement, board/shareholder resolutions, source of funds evidence, and updated register of shareholders. Corporate treasury must ensure the injection is credited to the designated capital account and then transferred to the operating account only as approved in the Quebec corporation's internal treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine outbound disbursements to foreign universities, licensed agents, government visa bodies, and service providers should use SWIFT MT103 with precise purpose codes and supporting invoices. For high-value prepayments where a bank undertaking is required, commercial letters of credit (advising or confirmation) under UCP600 are recommended. Escrow releases must be executed only against a written escrow instruction matching the underlying client agreement and immigration program requirements. Lynx (Payments Canada's RTGS system) is used for large-value Canadian-dollar clearing, while cross-border foreign-currency settlements settle via SWIFT/CHIPS corresponding banking. Every outgoing transfer over CAD 10,000 must be captured in the FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle) of the enterprise, including confirmation of the Register of Ultimate Beneficiaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: no later than the last day of the month following the month of each annual anniversary of initial registration (e.g., June 15 anniversary means July 31 deadline).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an increased tariff (approximately CAD 70-75 for a one-year late declaration); the REQ may publish a notice of default and, after continued non-compliance, proceed to strike-off or dissolution by publication, with corporate assets escheating to the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable only if the corporation is federally incorporated or is an extra-provincial CBCA entity registered in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation or registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an additional tariff (approximately CAD 20-40); continued failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years enables administrative dissolution by the Director under section 212 of the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end the filing deadline is June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default, capped at 12 months; a repeated-failure penalty of 10%; daily-compounding prescribed-rate interest; directors may be personally liable for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (CO-17 / financial data file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end the filing deadline is June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default, capped at 12 months, plus prescribed-rate daily interest; penalties mirror the CRA framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Summary of Remuneration Paid and RL-1 Annual Payroll Information Returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (T4) and Revenu Quebec (RL-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of February following the calendar year (February 29 in leap years).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty of CAD 25 per day for late filing of the T4 information return, to a maximum of CAD 7,500; Revenu Quebec imposes comparable RL-1 penalties and additional fines for wilful omissions or false statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM), statutory register updates, and minutes book maintenance (no external filing, but evidenced through the Annual Declaration and required by the Quebec Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and corporate records (internal governance; subject to REQ and CRA inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once per calendar year and no more than 15 months after the preceding AGM.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct registry fine, but failure to maintain statutory registers or to hold AGMs exposes directors to compliance orders and penalties under the QBCA and supports REQ or CRA non-compliance findings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset or revenue threshold applies under Quebec or federal corporate law: a non-reporting Quebec private corporation may waive the independent audit by shareholder consent under the QBCA. A mandate to appoint an auditor arises only if the corporation is a reporting issuer or distributing corporation, if the articles or a unanimous shareholder agreement require it, if shareholders exercise statutory audit rights, or if the professional regulator (CICC) imposes a financial review in disciplinary or compliance matters.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is mandatory for reporting issuers; private corporations may elect IFRS or ASPE (Part II). Financial statements must be sufficient to support T2/CO-17 computations, the REQ annual declaration, and CICC professional file-retention obligations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law requires each registered corporation to maintain a Register of Ultimate Beneficiaries (RUB). The register must be kept current and its accuracy confirmed with the REQ Annual Declaration; any change in ultimate beneficiary information must be declared to the REQ within 60 days of the corporation becoming aware of the change. The Annual Declaration is the annual UBO confirmation protocol.

stage_6.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), jurisdiction of incorporation, registered office, tax year-end. A business corporation in Quebec must also indicate its Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where directors are non-residents, the T2 must identify the corporate status (e.g., 100% foreign-controlled), the controlling foreign parent, and the place of central management. If central management is outside Canada, claim treaty tie-breaker relief and file Form T2 Sch. 4 to determine residency.
